objective: Build a polished, compact Godot tower-defense vertical slice where three workshop instruments create readable thermal reactions along one living fuse, culminating in a memorable furnace-warden boss.

context.label: Concept-only material and mood inspiration; not a gameplay or production target

nodes.instructions: Explore three-tower thermal-combo grammars, enemy counterplay, wave pacing, and meaningful upgrade choices for an eight-to-twelve-minute vertical slice. Preserve the one-fuse identity. Propose a bounded but surprising candidate, not a generic genre checklist.

Explore tactile placement, attack anticipation, reaction feedback, readable combat density, accessibility, onboarding, and the smallest useful audio vocabulary. Identify how the game can feel authored and juicy without hiding tactical state.

Develop contrasting wave arcs and a furnace-warden finale that force the player to reinterpret the same three instruments. Seek one memorable systemic twist that fits the existing compact Godot architecture.

Act as a lightweight Direction Auditor. Audit STYLE.md, visual-direction.json, the direction-maturity design system, Godot Theme, studies, and current implementation. Treat the legacy concept image only as material and mood inspiration. Identify a small set of high-leverage semantic gaps and an engine-feasible rendering hypothesis; do not build an asset library or regenerate studies before gameplay passes. Preserve creative latitude through semantic roles rather than frozen layouts.

Only after the gameplay gate passes, inspect the direction system, ImageGen studies, concept-only material reference, running graybox, and baseline captures with image-aware tools. Define one representative in-engine art slice at the shipping camera: one route bend, three sockets, one tower, one enemy, the heart, one HUD interaction, and one complete anticipation/action/impact/settle beat. Choose a feasible layered 2.5D Godot strategy and explicitly reject any concept-art qualities that cannot survive gameplay scale. Do not plan the whole asset library.

Synthesize one opinionated systems plan: combat grammar, teaching sequence, four-wave arc, boss twist, interaction contract, economy, deterministic evidence, and a bounded implementation plan. Keep presentation hooks semantic so a later visual specialist has room to explore.

Implement and verify the playable systems slice before visual polish. Keep title, build, four-wave, boss, victory/defeat/replay flows; make placement, reactions, economy, upgrades, and deterministic hooks correct and legible. Prefer extracting systems into src/ where practical. Preserve presentation seams for the visual specialist; do not spend the run on decorative polish.
Run the cheap engine-native load, fixture, fire, and telemetry contract before expensive polish.

Inspect and test for strategic degeneracy, unusable placement/upgrade flow, reaction bugs, stuck waves, boss failures, reset/progression bugs, boundary violations, and dishonest metrics. Return pass or revise with concrete evidence.

Turn the passed gameplay loop and visual-director handoff into a bounded vertical-art-slice brief. Specify the representative live-wave state, exact production surfaces to finish, engine resources to reuse, capture conditions, performance/readability risks, and explicit out-of-scope asset families. The slice proves a production method, not the whole game. Do not reopen passed systems decisions without concrete evidence.

Build only the representative production-quality art slice inside the already working Godot loop. Finish one route bend, three sockets, one tower, one enemy, the heart, one HUD interaction, and one complete anticipation/action/impact/settle beat at the shipping camera. Use project-bound sprites/textures, custom typography, lighting, shaders, particles, or code-native geometry according to the proven 2.5D strategy; code-native does not mean primitive-only. Preserve gameplay contracts. Do not expand every screen, tower, enemy, prop, or wave yet. At the end, run the engine capture, copy the representative gameplay capture into design/references/emberline-production-slice.png, and create design/production-slice.json describing the camera, implemented surfaces, reusable resources, deliberate omissions, and source capture. Update DESIGN_SYSTEM.md and exact design-system.json hashes; set maturity production-slice; add the capture with purpose gameplay, authority production-target, source captured; add the manifest as adapter godot-production-slice. Leave reusable resources and semantic seams for later expansion.
Run the cheap runtime contract after the bounded art slice and every slice repair.
Capture the deterministic live-wave art slice and seven-frame attack/reaction evidence from the running Godot project at the shipping camera. Other views remain diagnostic at this gate.

Confirm that the bounded art slice preserved the previously passed placement, reactions, economy, upgrades, deterministic hooks, wave progression, boss, reset, and replay behavior. Use runtime evidence and concrete state inspection. This is a regression gate, not an invitation to redesign the passed loop.

Gate the production method before visual expansion. Inspect the running live-wave slice and full motion sequence at gameplay scale. Judge material separation, silhouette, typography, interaction readability, motion, performance feasibility, and whether the resources can be reused. The legacy concept image is inspiration only and cannot supply gameplay evidence. Return pass only if this small slice looks authored and engine-feasible; otherwise return one bounded repair brief. Never require completion of out-of-scope screens or asset families, and never call proxy evidence fun.

Expand only the production vocabulary proven by the accepted art slice across the title, planning board, remaining towers and enemies, boss, victory/defeat, and replay. Reuse its resources, typography, material layers, camera assumptions, and motion grammar. Add assets only for proven gameplay roles; do not invent a second visual language or chase concept-art detail that failed the gameplay-scale gate. Preserve runtime contracts, accessibility, and deterministic hooks.
Re-run the runtime contract after production-vocabulary expansion and every final repair.
Capture deterministic title, board, live wave, and seven-frame attack/reaction evidence after full presentation expansion.

Act as a strict final visual/experience director. Inspect every still and the complete seven-frame motion sequence with image-aware tools. Use the captured production slice as the feasibility and visual-vocabulary target; use the legacy concept image only for material and mood inspiration; use baselines only to measure improvement. Pass only if the proven vocabulary expands coherently without harming gameplay readability. Always return findings.scorecard numeric 0-100 for material_depth, focal_hierarchy, combat_legibility, authored_specificity, composition_typography, motion_feedback. Always return findings.evidence with one object per required view containing view, path, and a concrete observation, plus one object with sequence tower-fire and a concrete temporal observation, plus findings.blockingIssues. Never inflate scores or call it fun without human playtest.
